chunks: My father (rah) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad who said: Abi narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Abdillah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever recites: 'Glory be to Allah and to Him be praise, Glory be to Allah the Great and to Him be praise,' Allah will record for him three thousand good deeds, erase from him three thousand bad deeds, and raise for him three thousand grades, and He will create from them a bird in Paradise that glorifies Allah, and the reward of its glorification will be for him.

key_terms.سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ الْعَظِیمِ: Glory be to Allah the Great
key_terms.سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَ بِحَمْدِهِ: Glory be to Allah and to Him be praise

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards for reciting Subhanallah wa bihamdihi Subhanallah al-Azimi wa bihamdihi?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A’mal*, this hadith highlights the immense spiritual economy of the specific dhikr 'Subhanallah wa bihamdihi, Subhanallah al-Azim,' linking verbal devotion to tangible metaphysical rewards. Beyond the numerical multiplication of deeds and ranks, the unique creation of a bird in Paradise symbolizes the enduring, active nature of one’s worship, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the continuity of reward (sadaqah jariyah) even after death. This narrative underscores the transformative power of consistent praise in purifying the soul and elevating the believer’s status in the hereafter.
